title: Finite open external-tensor comparison and signed factor swap
statement:
Use the finite coefficient datum $k,A=A_{E,n}$ of [def-pur-conventions]. Work in the ordinary unbounded constant-$A$ module derived categories on the small pro-etale sites, with pullback, derived tensor and signed symmetry $\sigma$ of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Let $\bar X,\bar Z,B,X,Z$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes, let $a:\bar X\to B$, $b:\bar Z\to B$ be separated finite-type morphisms, and let $j:X\hookrightarrow\bar X$, $k:Z\hookrightarrow\bar Z$ be open immersions [def-weil-open-immersion]. Set $C=\bar X\times_B\bar Z$, $P=X\times_BZ$, with projections $r,t$ on $C$ and $p,q$ on $P$, and $u=j\times_Bk:P\hookrightarrow C$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. For arbitrary $M\in D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ and $N\in D(Z_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ put
$$E=Lr^*j_!M\otimes_A^LLt^*k_!N,\qquad D=Lp^*M\otimes_A^LLq^*N,$$
using exact extension by zero [def-weil-extension-by-zero]. In the factorization $P\xrightarrow{w}X\times_B\bar Z\xrightarrow{v}C$ of $u$, define $e_{j,k}:E\to u_!D$ as follows: use open base change for $j$, then the open tensor comparison for $v$, then inside $v_!$ open base change for $k$ and the open tensor comparison for $w$ (using signed symmetry to place the extension factor first), and finally $v_!w_!\cong u_!$. All base-change and tensor maps are the actual unit-normalized maps of [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization]; tensor/pullback identifications are those of [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso], and open compositors those of [lem-cbc-extension-zero-composition]. Define $e^{\mathrm{op}}_{j,k}$ by the other factorization through $\bar X\times_BZ$. Then both maps are isomorphisms, their restrictions along $u$ are $1_D$ under the specified open units, and $e_{j,k}=e^{\mathrm{op}}_{j,k}$.

Put $C'=\bar Z\times_B\bar X$, $P'=Z\times_BX$, let $\bar s:C\xrightarrow{\sim}C'$ and $s:P\xrightarrow{\sim}P'$ be the swaps, and let $u':P'\hookrightarrow C'$. Transport the reversed construction $e_{k,j}$ by $\bar s^*$ and the normalized open base-change identifications, obtaining $\widetilde e_{k,j}:Lt^*k_!N\otimes_A^LLr^*j_!M\to u_!(Lq^*N\otimes_A^LLp^*M)$. The actual maps satisfy
$$e_{j,k}=u_!(\sigma_{Lq^*N,Lp^*M})\circ\widetilde e_{k,j}\circ\sigma_{Lr^*j_!M,Lt^*k_!N}.$$
No boundedness, etale-origin, constructibility, finite Tor-amplitude, properness of $a,b$, or abstract six-functor datum is assumed.
